chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One prays six rak'at for the Ihram, entering into Ihram after the last of them, and this does not contradict what has been narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: How many rak'at are performed for the Ihram prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar establishes the Sunnah of performing six rak'at of prayer before entering Ihram, a practice widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as a recommended act (Mustahabb) to purify the soul before the pilgrimage rites. The text notes the consistency of this ruling with other narrations, reflecting the scholarly effort to harmonize varying reports on the number of rak'at and the timing of the Ihram declaration within the chain of transmission from Imam al-Sadiq.
